title: Out of memory: what ComfyUI tries first

questions.q: A VAE decode runs out of memory. What does ComfyUI do?
options: Logs a warning and retries with tiles
questions.answer: Logs a warning and retries with tiles
questions.why: VAE.decode catches it and calls a tiled decode. The warning is in the source.

questions.q: Which part has no general retry of its own, in what we could find?
questions.why: Apart from the split attention retry, we found no fallback in comfy/samplers.py. So the error usually appears at the sampler.

questions.q: After an out of memory error reaches the engine, why is the next queue slower?
questions.why: execute() calls unload_all_models, so they load again.

questions.q: How does the upscale node's retry work?
options: Doubles the tile until it fits
Halves the tile from 512, and gives up below 128
questions.answer: Halves the tile from 512, and gives up below 128

questions.q: What is the first thing to check, according to ComfyUI's own tip?
questions.why: The tip says: you might have accidentally set the batch_size to a large number.

questions.q: The out of memory fallback tiles a 1024 square SD image at its default sizes. How many tile decodes?
questions.why: Three passes of 9, 7 and 7, from get_tiled_scale_steps and decode_tiled_, whose default overlap is 16. The VAEDecodeTiled node's default overlap is 8, which gives 19.
